question: How do I turn on Stellar's built-in fully-private, shielded-by-default transaction mode for all my payments?

golden.answer: There is no such mode: Stellar has no network-wide switch or account setting for shielded payments, and ordinary transactions are public. Privacy is opt-in through applications. As of 2026-11-14, Confidential Tokens hide balances and amounts but keep sender and receiver addresses public, and their verifier does not yet guarantee privacy; Stellar Private Payments is an unaudited Testnet developer preview.
keyFacts: Stellar has no global shielded-by-default mode or setting; ordinary activity is public.
Privacy is opt-in via applications; Confidential Tokens hide amounts but not addresses.
avoid: Do NOT invent an enablement command or claim Stellar is shielded by default.
Do NOT present unaudited Testnet previews as audited Mainnet products.
golden.notes: Cryptographic primitives (CAP-0059, CAP-0074/0075) are not a privacy mode. Do not credit a claim that a public observer can recover every amount from chain data. Example as of 2026-11-14: Stellar Private Payments is an unaudited Testnet developer preview; accept a later dated status.

GT-25 CORRECTION 2026-07-10: no global privacy toggle exists, but current optional applications can hide defined fields. Grade ordinary/default transparency plus explicit product network, audit, and visibility status; BN254/Poseidon are live P25 primitives, not a turnkey mode.

REFRESH 2026-11-02: Confidential Tokens v0.8.0 contracts are audited and called Mainnet-ready, but the verifier accepts only non-zero-knowledge proofs. An answer that reports this limit does not fire the visibility avoid. The designated auditor can decrypt amounts by design. Do not credit a claim that a public observer can recover every amount from proofs or chain data; the sources say only that further leakage is not ruled out.
